title: Space-query exponent curve of gapped string indexing
formal:
Determine the dimensionless space exponent \(s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)\) for every real \(\delta\in[0,1]\). For each such \(\delta\), let
\[
s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)=\inf\{s\in[1,\infty):\ \forall\eta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\ \exists\mathcal D,K,C_0,h,d\text{ satisfying the bounds below}\}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal D=(P,Q)\) is a uniform randomized static indexing scheme in the stated word-RAM model, \(K,C_0\ge1\) are constants, and \(h\ge1,d\ge8\) are integers. For every \(n\ge2\), every length-\(n\) text, and every valid query, preprocessing takes at most \(C_0(n+2)^h\) steps; the index together with query workspace uses at most \(Kn^{s+\eta}\) words; and the query takes at most
\[
K\bigl(m_1+m_2+n^{\delta+\eta}(1+\mathrm{occ})\bigr)
\]
steps. Each bound holds for every outcome of the random choices. For each fixed text and query, the complete output is correct with probability at least \(2/3\), over preprocessing and query randomness. The chosen programs and constants may depend on \(\delta,s,\eta\), but not on the text, its length, or a query. The requested answer is a real-valued function \(g\) on \([0,1]\), certified to satisfy \(\lvert g(\delta)-s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)\rvert\le1/100\) at every point.
definitions:
The input text is an explicit array \(T[0],\ldots,T[n-1]\), with each entry in \(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\). A query consists of two explicit nonempty arrays \(P_1,P_2\) over the same alphabet, their lengths \(1\le m_1,m_2\le n\), and integers \(0\le a\le b<n\). A start \(i\) for \(P_1\) is valid when \(0\le i\le n-m_1\) and \(T[i+u]=P_1[u]\) for every \(0\le u<m_1\); define starts \(j\) for \(P_2\) analogously. The answer is the set of all ordered pairs \((i,j)\) of valid starts with \(a\le j-i\le b\). Each pair must be written exactly once, in any order, followed by termination. Overlapping occurrences and \(i=j\) are allowed when they satisfy the conditions. The true cardinality of this set is \(\mathrm{occ}\), even when evaluating the time bound on an unsuccessful random outcome. The gap measures start-to-start distance, not the number of characters between two nonoverlapping occurrences. Both gap endpoints arrive with the query.

Preprocessing \(P\) receives \(n\) and the explicit text and produces a finite stored index. Query program \(Q\) receives \(n\), that index, and the explicit query. The text is available during a query only to the extent it was retained in charged index memory. The index is static and read-only during a query. Each query starts with empty working memory and no input-dependent private state from earlier queries. Random words used at different steps are independent and uniform; retained preprocessing randomness is accessible only through the stored index. Success is required separately for every fixed text/query pair; a single preprocessing outcome need not answer all possible queries simultaneously, and no guarantee against queries selected after inspecting private random choices is imposed. Time and space bounds are worst-case, not expected or amortized.

The machine is a sequential word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\). Its programs have finite descriptions and a fixed finite number of registers and instructions. Input integers and symbols are supplied as ordinary words; \(n,m_1,m_2,a,b\) are included. Unit-cost instructions are reading or writing one addressed word, copying, comparison, branching, Boolean operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and integer quotient or remainder with a nonzero divisor. Logical shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Generating one independent uniform \(w\)-bit word costs one instruction. Addresses and individual stored values must fit a word. Computations on larger integers pay for all constituent instructions. There is no advice, input-dependent oracle, free random function, or uncharged table.

All initialization, reads, writes, random generation, table construction, and output writes count toward the time of the phase in which they occur. Preprocessing workspace is charged to preprocessing time and is therefore polynomially bounded; it need not satisfy the smaller retained-space bound. Every retained word counts toward index space, including stored text, metadata, tables, seeds and registers retained between phases. During a query, that space bound additionally counts all registers and working memory. Only the read-only current query and the streamed output are excluded from storage, and writing the output is charged to query time. Finite control is part of the fixed program, not a source of size-dependent advice. The constants, register count and polynomial preprocessing degree are fixed once \(\delta,s,\eta\) are chosen.

The quantifiers allow different finite programs for different parameter choices and different positive rational slack values. They do not require a computable procedure that takes an arbitrary real \(\delta\) or \(s\) and constructs a program, and those real numbers are never supplied to a machine. The slack defines exponents rather than hidden fixed logarithmic factors. The infimum is finite and need not be attained; the target does not demand a scheme at exactly the optimal exponent without slack. The normalization \(s\ge1\), full domain \([0,1]\), polynomial preprocessing and inclusion of query workspace retain the card's selected convention.

context_blocks.text: The original paper asks whether simultaneous subquadratic storage and sublinear query overhead are possible and answers that question affirmatively. The present card retains the user-approved editorial extension to the optimal exponent curve; it is not a restatement of that already answered binary question.

Theorem 1 reports space \(\widetilde O(n^{2-\delta/3})\) or \(\widetilde O(n^{3-2\delta})\), with query time \(\widetilde O(m_1+m_2+n^\delta(1+\mathrm{occ}))\). Its reporting definition uses the same ordered start-distance convention. The tilde hides polylogarithmic factors; Section 5 separately explains linear dependence on the pattern lengths.

The April 2026 revision of the implicit-set-search paper recovers the first of these tradeoffs and extends the types of queries. Its literal substring definition uses absolute distance between starts, so that formulation must be distinguished from the ordered pairs selected here.

The April 2026 3SUM-indexing paper improves a different indexing tradeoff and explicitly derives a Jumbled Indexing consequence. It does not state an improved gapped-reporting curve. The previous card text claiming improvements in some parameter regimes for this curve was unsupported by that citation and has been corrected.

Polynomial preprocessing, bounded error per fixed query, worst-case resource limits, charged query workspace and the numerical accuracy target are the card’s explicit editorial conventions. The checked literature does not independently establish that this exact approximation target remains open.

why: An optimal storage-versus-query curve would identify the limits of reusing a preprocessed text for paired-pattern searches with query-dependent distance constraints. This is a basic indexing primitive motivated by motif searches and co-occurrence analysis.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function \(g:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) and a complete mathematically correct Lean proof that \(\lvert g(\delta)-s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)\rvert\le1/100\) for every real \(\delta\in[0,1]\), in exactly the stated uniform model. A proved interval of width at most \(1/50\) at every point qualifies through its midpoint; exact determination also qualifies. The representation may be a mathematical expression or a certified evaluation rule, but merely renaming the defining infimum is insufficient. A plot, finitely many samples, or a one-sided bound does not determine the entire curve to the required precision. This numerical acceptance tolerance does not assert resolution of a distinct exact threshold conjecture.

The implicit-set-search revision gives a general framework recovering a gapped-string tradeoff and treating additional query types.
The revised 3SUM-indexing paper improves 3SUM and Jumbled Indexing bounds; its stated string consequence is not an improved curve for this card.

sentences: A query supplies two patterns and an interval of allowed distances between their starting positions in a fixed text.
The index must report every ordered pair of matching starts in the interval, including valid overlaps.
The target is the optimal stored-space exponent throughout a fixed range of query-overhead exponents.
Uniform programs have polynomial preprocessing, bounded error for each fixed query, and worst-case bounds counting query workspace.
The original 2024 binary question was answered positively; this editorial curve requires certified real-valued accuracy of 1/100 at every point.

checked_sources: Read actual arXiv2211.16860v2 PDF, version5March2024 (internal heading6March): introduction pp1–2 explicitly answers its binary question; Theorem1 states both curves. Section5 pp11–12 gives exact start-distance reporting, random perfect-hash access for linear pattern dependence, and generic witness-returning Shifted Set Intersection transfer in Theorem7. Theorem6 p6 reduces SSI to3SUM. Tilde notation in a theorem is not automatically the exact card query expression; Section5 separates the pattern term.

The feasible set is nonempty with finite infimum under the strict model: finite polynomial tabulation of all distinct substrings, pairs and gap intervals gives a finite polynomial-size index with linear pattern lookup and output time. This elementary finiteness audit is not presented as a solver recipe or as an optimal bound. Preprocessing memory differs from stored/query memory in the retained interpretation.

Read arXiv2311.12471v2, latest landing-page revision22April2026: Theorem9 p8 reports distinct domain preimages, Theorem13 p9 recovers the2-alpha/3 curve. Its literal Problem3 uses absolute distance. A direct signed adaptation would use f(p,q)=(p,q,SA[q]-SA[p]+n) in Theorem9 and the relevant query box; merely filtering absolute-distance answers could violate output sensitivity. This is an editorial transfer observation, not a claim that the literal definition matches. No proof-assistant verification or full implementation audit was performed.

Read actual arXiv2512.04258v2, revision23April2026: Theorem1 improves3SUM tradeoff TS~n^2.5 in its stated range. Corollary4 printedpp4,16 (PDFpp5,17) and Theorem3.8 printedp11 concern Jumbled Indexing. The former progress sentence was therefore corrected.
